title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 9 Oct 2026]
Title:LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:Corpus-level long-context reasoning requires agents to acquire and integrate evidence across document collections that exceed their context windows. Existing agent harnesses enable incremental access to these corpora, but acquired evidence and evolving conclusions often remain entangled in a growing interaction history. This implicit state management can lead to two coupled failure modes: unbounded exploration, where retrieval expands the interaction history without resolving decision-relevant information gaps, and evidence-state drift, where previously acquired evidence or subsequent corrections fail to inform the current conclusion. We present LongHarness, a model-agnostic harness that makes the interaction between acquired evidence and evolving conclusions explicit. Its core mechanism, Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution, uses unresolved conclusions to guide exploration toward missing information, while newly acquired evidence strengthens or revises the conclusions that directed the search. LongHarness couples this process with Evidence Lifecycle Management, which keeps accumulated evidence current and traceable throughout the interaction. Together, these mechanisms focus retrieval on remaining information needs and keep conclusions aligned with current evidence. We evaluate LongHarness on OfficeQA Pro V1 and V2, AA-LCR, and LongBench v2 using GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash. Compared with direct reasoning using the same backbone, LongHarness improves GLM-5.3-Flash exact match on OfficeQA Pro from 15.8% to 60.2% on V1 and from 4.4% to 61.1% on V2. Against state-of-the-art agent harnesses, it surpasses Claude Code by 12.0 percentage points on V1 and Codex by 18.9 points on V2. With Qwen3.8-Flash, LongHarness reaches 61.7% on V1, outperforming Claude Code by 8.3 points and Codex by 12.0 points.

report.summary: LongHarness introduces explicit evidence-state management to help agents reason over 100M-token corpora, sharply improving long-context QA accuracy over direct reasoning and leading agent harnesses.
report.background: As enterprise and research document collections grow past 100 million tokens, agents must integrate evidence far beyond their context windows. Existing agent harnesses can retrieve incrementally, but evidence and evolving conclusions often remain tangled in a growing interaction history. This implicit state management creates two coupled failures: unbounded exploration, where retrieval expands history without resolving information gaps, and evidence-state drift, where earlier evidence or corrections fail to inform the current conclusion. LongHarness responds with a model-agnostic harness that makes the relationship between acquired evidence and evolving conclusions explicit, aiming to keep retrieval focused and conclusions aligned as reasoning proceeds.
key_points: LongHarness centers on Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution: unresolved conclusions guide exploration toward missing information, while newly acquired evidence strengthens or revises the conclusions that directed the search. This creates a feedback loop between retrieval and reasoning rather than treating them as separate stages.

Evidence Lifecycle Management keeps accumulated evidence current and traceable throughout the interaction. It addresses stale, duplicated, or contradictory evidence so that later decisions remain grounded in the best available information instead of an increasingly noisy history.

On OfficeQA Pro with GLM-5.3-Flash, LongHarness raises exact match from 15.8% to 60.2% on V1 and from 4.4% to 61.1% on V2. It surpasses Claude Code by 12.0 points on V1 and Codex by 18.9 points on V2.

With Qwen3.8-Flash, LongHarness reaches 61.7% on OfficeQA Pro V1, outperforming Claude Code by 8.3 points and Codex by 12.0 points. Results across two backbones suggest the harness is model-agnostic rather than tuned to one model.

The evaluation spans OfficeQA Pro V1 and V2, AA-LCR, and LongBench v2, targeting corpus-level long-context reasoning. The focus is not just larger context windows but stateful evidence management across document collections that exceed any single context window.
report.impact: LongHarness signals a shift from simply expanding context windows toward managing agent state explicitly. For the AI industry, it suggests harness design and evidence lifecycle management may matter as much as backbone model scale. For developers, it offers a model-agnostic pattern for building more reliable long-context agents without retraining models, potentially reducing hallucinations and wasted retrieval. For regular users, the practical effect could be more trustworthy document analysis in legal, financial, medical, and enterprise search workflows, where agents must track many sources over long interactions. If adopted, such methods could make AI assistants better at citing, correcting, and updating conclusions as new evidence appears.
report.tools: Follow the LongHarness paper on arXiv and its experimental HTML version; alphaXiv and Hugging Face Papers can help track discussion and code. Related open-source directions include LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and Haystack for agentic retrieval; Letta/MemGPT and Zep for memory and state; GraphRAG for structured evidence. For evaluation, watch LongBench v2, AA-LCR, and OfficeQA Pro. Claude Code and Codex are useful baselines to compare harness behavior.
